findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil buildup in the dish machine. The dish machine was supposed to have been cleaned as per discussion during the last inspection. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure that the accumulated soil buildup is cleaned and the dish machine is maintained cleaned to sight of touch at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning a new pair of gloves.The employee carried out multiple tasks; one of which involved the handling of raw meat. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure employees always wash their hands prior to donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a container filled with raw cut steak being stored over raw fish in the second prep cooler. The PIC was made aware. The items in question were rearranged to correct the storage order. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Two sani buckets (one in the kitchen and one at the bar) were observed with a quaternary ammonia sanitizer concentration reading between 100 ppm to 0 ppm. The staff were instructed to remake the sanitizer buckets. The buckets were remade and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of sanitizers are routinely checked to ensure proper sanitation for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: REPEAT Inspector observed knives to be stored in the gap between two prep coolers. This space is not considered easily cleanable and is therefore not adequate for utensil storage. The knives were sent to dish during the inspection. Inspector recommends a magnetic strip or alternative knife storage.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed salmon in the walk-in cooler to be thawed in its original reduced oxygen packaging. The packaging bore a label indicating that the packaging had to be opened prior to thawing. Education was conducted regarding the risks of thawing fish in reduced oxygen packaging. The packages were opened during the inspection. Ensure staff are opening the packaging prior to thawing to prevent the growth of clostridium botulinum, the organism that causes botulism toxicity.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspectors observed no food protection manager (CFPM) present during food preparation and service. The PIC was informed that a CFPM needs to present at all times of food prep or service. Ensure staff have certification prior to next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two sanitizer buckets in the kitchen measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The dispenser was tested as well, measuring 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The inspectors discovered that the detergent and sanitizer were swapped in the dispenser. Due to this mistake, the buckets were filled with a detergent solution rather than sanitizer. The bottles were swapped and the dispenser was flushed. The dispenser then measured 150ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. Ensure staff are measuring the concentration of sanitizer buckets frequently to catch when these mistakes happen and correct them. Test strips are kept at the bar for safe keeping.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a stainless steel cup and scoop next to the server’s ice bin to be soiled and retaining old water. The PIC was informed and the cup and scoop were moved to the dish area. Ensure staff are washing and sanitizing these items frequently to prevent cross-contamination with ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed large containers of commercial teriyaki and sweet chili to be stored on a shelf in the kitchen. These containers stated “refrigerate after opening” on the manufacturer’s label. The PIC was informed and these containers were discarded. Ensure refrigeration requirements from the manufacturer are followed at all times. 

***Labels stating “for best flavor, refrigerate after opening” does not state a requirement. This is for flavor and quality, not safety.***
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspectors noted the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to be missing a date mark:
1. Beef sticks in walk-in
2. Cubed cheese in walk-in
3. Celery in walk-in
4. Egg mix in walk-in (only opened containers kept longer than 24 hours need marked)
5. Blue cheese in walk-in
6. Mexican blend cheese in walk-in
7. Cooked corn in walk-in
8. White gravy in walk-in
9. Wet batter in walk-in 
10. Corned beef in walk-in
11. Roughly 6-8 unlabeled containers of food in walk-in

Inspectors observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to be kept longer than their 7-day date mark:
1. Mashed potato in left prep cooler, dated 12/4
2. Brisket in right prep cooler, dated 12/3
3. Celery in right prep cooler, dated 12/2
4. Cauliflower in right prep cooler, dated 12/2
5. Boneless wings in right prep cooler, dated 11/21
6. Ranch in server cooler, dated 12/9

All items stored beyond their date were discarded. Ensure staff are monitoring coolers and dating foods kept in cooler longer than 24 hours after preparation or opening. Ensure also that staff are discarding any food items beyond their 7-day date mark (the date marked on the container counts as day 1). A follow-up is scheduled for 12/26/2025 to ensure date marking is corrected in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed no stem (probe) thermometer in use in the kitchen during food preparation. The PIC was informed and could not find a stem thermometer in the facility. A follow-up is scheduled for 12/26/2025 to ensure a stem thermometer is acquired.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple containers of food in the walk-in cooler to not be labeled with their common name. Ensure food is clearly marked for monitoring purposes and to avoid confusion or misuse.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed a significant buildup of ice in the walk-in freezer on the ceilings, as well as the air curtains and floors. The walk-in cooler must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ice falling from the ceiling of the cooler poses a cross-contamination hazard. Ensure that the walk-in freezer frost is removed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following physical facilities in need of repair: 
1. Cove base next to the mop sink is broken and partially missing
2. Protective coating on new steam table is peeling. Peel off coating to make equipment smooth and easily cleanable.
3. The back door of the facility is improperly sealed (daylight is visible through the bottom seal)
4. Moisture damage is observed on the wall to the left of the walk-in cooler. Seal wall and protect against future moisture with either waterproof sealant or Nudo paneling.

Ensure these facility repairs are complete prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated on the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning a new pair of gloves. The employee had just finished handling a bleach solution that was too strong for food contact surfaces. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure employees always wash their hands prior to donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an employee spraying cutting boards and other food contact surfaces with an unlabeled bottle of bleach solution. The solution was tested, and “bleached out” the test strip. Bleaching out the strip is an indicator that the solution is far stronger than the maximum indication of the strip, which is 200ppm. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer was far too strong and should not be used on food-contact surfaces. Quaternary ammonia tablets were used to prepare a new sanitizer solution. Ensure staff use test strips to measure the concentration of a sanitizing solution prior to spraying on food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple containers in the walk-in cooler (including cooked beef) to be missing a date mark. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must be marked with a date mark and discarded within 7 days of opening/preparation. Ensure all foods are marked prior to storing overnight in the walk-in cooler. A follow-up will be conducted on October 10, 2025 to ensure facility is in compliance for date marking.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: Inspector observed skirt steak on the menu which is served undercooked. The menu had no consumer advisory statement, and there was no statement posted visibly in the facility. The PIC was informed of the need for a consumer advisory statement and signage was provided. Ensure this disclaimer is visible to the public at all times of undercooked or raw food service.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.

findings.citation_text: 7-101.11 Identifying Information, Prominence. Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there is a significant buildup of ice in the walk-in freezer on the ceilings, as well a slight accumulation on the air curtains and floors. The walk-in freezer must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the walk-in freezer frost is removed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is a buildup of dust and other debris on the white shelves above the triple sink. Non food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food reside, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves above the triple sink are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.comment:
4-601.11: The facility has a fan blowing that is heavily soiled with food debris and dust. Clean the fan and maintain all fans clean as the blow air through the facility that contacts food. Fan was being cleaned at time of inspection.

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The facility has a prep cooler that is in need of a thermostat. The facility knows this and has the thermostat in hand. They are waiting for the technician to come and do the work. The technician should be here tonight or tomorrow. Do not use this pre table for the cold holding of any food that requires temperature control for safety (TCS food). That would be proteins, cooked plant foods, cheese, house made dressings among other things. All TCS foods were discarded from the unit. The foods were 56F internally. Chicken salad, hard cooked eggs, tomatoes, noodles and cheeses along with dressings in the bottom of the unit and salad mix. If needed, set ups from the prep top that need temperature control for safety can be held on a proper ice bath. Proper ice bath is ice up to around the level of the food on all sides and the bottom. All TCS items were voluntarily discarded. The ice bath was discussed with the kitchen staff before the inspector left the facility. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the can opener to be soiled with dry food debris. Wash rinse and sanitize food contact surfaces any time they are contaminated. The can opener was cleaned and sanitized before open. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed frost accumulation on the walk in freezer ceiling and the small kitchen reach in freezer. Clean and maintain free of accumulated ice for the next routine inspection. The freezer in the kitchen is slated to be replaced. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Inspector observed two employees have beverages in the kitchen that were not handled properly. One open top cup had a straw but was also on the table at dish with clean dishes. The other beverage container was stored on a shelf above food and was a flip top/thermos style container with no straw.  Use a container with a lid and a straw to prevent contamination of the container and hands when drinking. Also, make sure that beverage containers are stored low and away from food and food related items.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

The dish machine is testing at 0 ppm of chlorine. The facility is going to wash, and rinse in the dish machine and then put dishes in the three part sink at 200ppm quat sanitizer for one minute of contact time. The dishes will be air dried. The machine will receive a follow up to see ensure that the correction has been made.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Inspector observed two wet wiping cloth buckets with 10ppm or les of quaternary ammonia sanitizer. Make sure to run the sanitizer dispenser until the foam is gone before filling the clean sanitizer bucket. Wet microfiber cloths with sanitizer from the dispenser before adding the cloths to the sanitizer buckets so that sanitizer does not bind to the cloth and is available to sanitize surfaces. The inspector trained the manager on duty on the method of making sanitizer buckets. Pass training along to all staff. Violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Inspector observed cheese sauce on the hot holding table at 128F. The cheese sauce was heated on the stove top according to the kitchen staff. They have a second set heating at time of inspection. The sauce has been on the steam table for about 2 hours. The cheese sauce is being reheated to 165F. The water level in the double pan was low for both containers of cheese sauce. The  water level was adjusted. Take care to properly use hot holding equipment. Take verification temperatures on food regularly throughout the day. Use the probe thermometer. Violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Inspector observed the floor drain at the hand sink in the kitchen is soiled heavily. Also the floor and walls on wither side of the walk in cooler door (on the outside) are soiled. Clean these area and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  

Observed chili that is a reheat to be in the hot holding well for reheating. The chili was moved to the grill top and reached 119F within half an hour. The chili was moved to the stove top on a double boiler and reheated to 165F. The violation is considered corrected at the time of inspection. Make sure to start reheats early enough to properly conduct the process.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed wet wiping cloths to be scattered on surfaces in the kitchen. Make every effort to keep wet cloths for wiping in sanitizer buckets when not actively using the cloth.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed bar hand sink to have a metal container with mixed drinks dumped into it (ice, straws, sliced fruits) within the basin of the hand sink. The hand sink is blocked from appropriate hand washing. Cease practice. Ensure hand sinks are accessible at all times for hand washing. Hand sinks are for hand washing ONLY. Ensure staff is aware. Discussed with PIC. COS - container was moved by the Inspector in order to wash hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas to have improper sanitization levels: kitchen 3 compartment sink, kitchen sani bucket, and dish machine. 3 compartment sink was 50-100 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Dish washer drained the, “sanitize”, basin and refilled it properly - 400 ppm. Sanitizer bucket in the kitchen was 0 ppm of quat. Sani bucket was remade - 400 ppm. Discussed frequent changes in sanitizer with dish washer and PIC. Ensure staff is changing sani buckets and the, “sanitize”, basin of the 3 compartment sink as frequently as needed to maintain 200-400 ppm.

Observed the dish machine to be 0 ppm. Multiple runs were conducted - 0 ppm. Machine was re-primed - still 0 ppm. Representative for the dish machine was called during the inspection. This is a frequent issue with the facility dish machine. PIC attempted to test dish machine himself with own test strips - multiple 0 ppm runs. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 8/2/22. Inspector will follow-up on 12/22/22. Utilize 3 compartment sink for ware washing until the dish machine is properly dispensing chlorine bleach - 50 to 200 ppm.

Facility has test strips for both types of sanitizer to check concentrations.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following food-contact areas to be in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. The warmer grates between the server area and the kitchen have food splash caked onto the grates. Repeat from 8/2/22 inspection.
2. There is mesh padding beneath the prep table in the walk-in cooler/freezer area with dirt/debris on it. Clean utensils (potato ricer, basins, etc.) are being placed on this. Clean the mesh passing and re-wash, rinse, sanitize the cooking equipment.
3. Both bottom prep coolers have significant food debris and splash on the edges of the shelving within (in the very back below the top portions of the prep coolers). 
4. The base of the reach-in cooler in the kitchen has food splash.

Ensure all areas are cleaned. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean the mentioned areas as needed to prevent food-contact surfaces being dirty. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 12/30/22.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed reduced oxygen packaging fish (ROP) - salmon - to be thawed within the packaging in the bottom of the second prep cooler. The packaging states to remove the fish before thawing. Discussed with cook and PIC. Ensure staff is aware to remove the salmon (or any other ROP fish that bares such a label) prior to thawing. Discussed wrapping fish in syran wrap individually. PIC and cook were in agreement. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers in the kitchen to be missing thermometers within the coolers. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer within. Discussed with PIC. PIC had additional thermometers on hand. COS. Ensure staff replaces thermometers as needed.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed the cups at the server station to be stacked wet. Cease practice. Cups should be air dried before being stacked. Ensure staff is aware (including dish washer). Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 8/2/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The vents above the grill lines are dusty - clean. Repeat from last routine inspection son 3/17/22 and 8/2/22.
2. The interior of the fryers (door and inside) are covered in a thick layer of grease and build-up - clean. Repeat from 8/2/22 inspection.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean the above mentioned areas as needed to prevent build-up of dust, debris, and grease. Clean before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

Observed mold on cooked noodles. Date marking indicated today was day 7 of time frame. Discard voluntarily. Ensure staff is aware to check foods, especially at Day 7. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

Observed employee remove 1 glove, text with cell phone, then attempt to re-engage in food behaviors (prep). Discussed with employee to wash hands. Employee rinsed hands in 3 compartment sink, then went outside. Came back into kitchen, donned gloves. No hand washing at the hand sink occurred. Cease practice. Wash hands properly after cell phone use. Don new gloves. Wash hands after entering the kitchen, before engaging in food manipulation. COS.

Discussed proper hand washing with PIC and glove use. Turn hand sink faucet handles off with barrier such as paper towel.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

Observed to-go containers used for dressing to be utilized as scoops within the chicken salad and the ranch dressing (metal containers within the bottom prep cooler). Cease practice. Scoops should have handles to minimize contact with ready-to-eat foods and prevent cross contamination. Discussed with head cook. COS.

Discussed with both CFPM’s present (cook and bar tender). Instructed facility to utilize the 3 compartment sink until the dish machine can be serviced and/or fixed. Inspector will follow-up on 8/5/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas to be in need of cleaning:
1. Ice machine interior baffle (major ice machine near the walk-in cooler/freezer) to have mold. Showed multiple employees and sent photos to the owner. Ice machine had recently been serviced per owner and multiple employees. 
2. The shelf above the 3 compartment sink has food splash along the grates and wall. The food- and lip-contact areas of the cookware are flipped onto this shelving unit. 
3. Interior and exterior of microwave has food splash and is not clean to touch.
4. The warmer grates between the server area and kitchen have food splash.
5. The prep knives are being stored in between the two prep coolers. Cease practice. Not a clean area to keep knives between use. Discussed with head cook.
6. Interior fan of the reach-in cooler (next to kitchen hand sink) has dust on vents.

Discussed with both CFPM’s present. Ensure staff is aware of routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces - wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 8/12/22.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed both prep coolers to be out of temperature. Multiple foods were probed (pork, beef patties, ranch dressing, chicken salad, mashed potatoes) and all items were roughly between 49 to 55 degrees F. Lunch rush had just ended and the coolers were likely being utilized and the top lids open. Prep coolers were turned down in temperature. All time/temperature controlled food (proteins, dairy, cut leafy greens, sliced/diced tomatoes) were moved to the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. Coolers should be monitored before dinner service and checked to see if the coolers are cold holding at 41 degrees F (dropped in temperature). These coolers have historically had cold holding issues (with previous owner as well). Coolers need to keep 41 degrees F or below even during busy rush services. Discussed with both CFPM’s present. Inspector suggested keeping the cooler set at a lower temperature generally and/or having someone service the equipment. Inspector will follow-up on 8/5/22.

Observed multiple stacks of cups at the server area before the kitchen to be improperly dried - cups are being stacked wet. Cease practice. Cups should be air dried prior to stacking. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware of proper drying practices.

A way to contain the water/sanitizer needs to be rectified without the use of a rag. Discussed with both CFPM’s. Service the 3 compartment sink so an appropriate part is put on the basin to hold sanitizer/water correctly.

(C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple employees to have in-use rags not submerged in sani buckets and laying on counters. Facility is using spray bottles and should be utilizing paper towels to wipe counters. PIC indicated he is likely switching back to sani buckets to keep in-use rags in those instead of the paper towel method. Ensure proper concentration of whatever type of sanitizer will be utilized in the sani buckets. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 8/6/21.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed left prep cooler to be out of temperature - maintaining roughly 55 to 63 degrees F. These temperatures were taken after lunch rush while the top prep cooler was open most of the time. Discussed with PIC importance of maintaining cooler temp at 41 degrees F or lower even during lunch and dinner rushes. All food in cooler (salad, sauces [including dairy based], pre-portioned noodles, and toppings [shred cheese, pickled onions, cut leafy greens, hard boiled eggs, etc.]) were carted to the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. This prep cooler has historically maintained marginal or high temperatures after a lunch and dinner rush. PIC called for service of cooler during inspection. Inspector will spot check cooler temperatures.
